subject: SLO readout and customer script transfer — CloudTide load-window coordination
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Morrison <ava@cloudtide.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLO readout and customer script transfer — CloudTide load-window coordination

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the clear constraints from your side. Quick recap from our end so we have aligned goals before the customer-led run:

- SLO targets you confirmed on the call: p95 end-to-end latency <= 300 ms for text generation (typical request size ~ 64 tokens), sustained throughput target ~ 350 req/s for the gateway tier. For streaming endpoints we noted a target of <= 20 ms per-token downstream latency under concurrency.
- Streaming concurrency target we captured as 120 concurrent clients, but flagged this for you to confirm (I called out 150 as an upper bound if you anticipate spikes).
- We prepared a starter k6 script (attached) that exercises both short-generation and streaming flows plus a simple KV-cache warmup.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Please confirm the test window that works for CloudTide operations: Jul 7 09:00–11:00 PT or Jul 9 21:00–23:00 PT. We can do a dry run in Redwood staging earlier if you want (recommended).
2) Confirm final concurrency number (120 vs 150). If you choose 150 we will update the script and recommend a slightly longer ramp.
3) Share IPs to allowlist for the test — attached is our allowlist template (ip_allowlist_template.csv).
4) Once windows and concurrency are locked, Marissa (cc'd) will push an updated script and coordinate a smoke test on our staging cluster; Vivek (ops) will be on-call for the test.

Attachments: cloudtide_k6_script_v1.js (k6 script stub), ip_allowlist_template.csv, mutual_action_plan_CloudTide.pdf

If that all looks right, reply with the window you prefer and the final concurrency number and we'll take it from there.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ava Morrison <ava@cloudtide.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cloudtide.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO readout and customer script transfer — CloudTide load-window coordination

Thanks, Karthik — that summary is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:  

- We want to land on p95 <= 350 ms (end-to-end) rather than 300 to give some buffer for payload variance.
- Streaming concurrency: we expect realistic peak concurrency to be ~150; can you confirm Redwood can sustain 150 clients for the streaming endpoint with per-token latency below ~25 ms? The per-token <20 ms target is optimistic for our worst-case clients.
- Throughput: we'll aim for 400 req/s as the peak probe for the gateway to validate autoscaling.

Preferred window: Jul 9 21:00–23:00 PT (off-hours for us). We will open a short maintenance window internally and route traffic accordingly.

I've attached our internal runbook link (we keep it internal but shared with ops@cloudtide.com) and I've populated your allowlist template with the minimal IPs we can provide from our VPN — however our security team prefers the explicit hostlist rather than CIDR ranges. I'll follow up with the exact host IPs by EOD tomorrow.

Also: can Redwood provide a short-term test API key scoped to a single project? We don't want to run against our prod keys for obvious reasons.

Thanks — Ava
Ava Morrison
CloudTide — Head of SRE
[attachment: cloudtide_runbook_internal.link.txt]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Morrison <ava@cloudtide.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO readout and customer script transfer — CloudTide load-window coordination

Ava — perfect, thanks for the direction. Short replies inline:  

- p95 <= 350 ms: noted and we'll target that for acceptance.
- Streaming concurrency 150: we can support that; Marissa will update the k6 script to set the streaming probe to 150 concurrent virtual users and extend the ramp to 15 minutes. That will also toggle the chunked streaming path to better reflect your client behavior.
- Peak probe throughput 400 req/s: pulling that into the test matrix. We'll include a steady-state 15-minute plateau at 400 rps and one 5-minute spike at 600 rps to validate autoscaling and graceful degradation.
- Short-term test API key: yes — we can provision a scoped test key for the run. Marissa, can you create the staging key and share TTL (suggest 48 hours) and masked credentials to Ava?

Marissa: can you take the attached cloudtide_k6_script_v1.js, make the two changes (concurrency=150, 15m ramp/15m plateau with a spike), and return a v2 script by EOD today? Please also do a dry-run on Redwood staging and post results to the Drive folder (link below). Vivek, please confirm you can be on-call for Jul 9 20:30–23:30 to help with toggles and any quick rollbacks.

Quoted for context:
> From: Ava Morrison <ava@cloudtide.com>
> We want to land on p95 <= 350 ms... Streaming concurrency: we expect realistic peak concurrency to be ~150... We'll aim for 400 req/s as the peak probe...

Thanks all — looking forward to the run.
Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Morrison <ava@cloudtide.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO readout and customer script transfer — CloudTide load-window coordination

Hi Ava / Karthik — quick update:  

- I updated the k6 script and attached cloudtide_k6_script_v2.js. Changes: concurrency set to 150, ramp-up 15m, plateau 15m at 400 rps, 5m spike to 600 rps. Added chunked-streaming probe that emits per-token timings and a warmup phase for KV caching.
- Provisioned a staging API key for CloudTide: test_key_CLOUDTIDE_**** (TTL 48 hours). I'll share the masked key and one-time retrieval link via the Drive access note (for security reasons we won't paste the full key in thread).
- Dry-run on Redwood staging completed this morning; summary CSV is in the Drive folder (link above). Key observations: 95th percentile latency at plateau averaged 320 ms for text-gen with the current model variant; streaming per-token median 18 ms and 95th at ~26 ms during spike — this matches the expectation you flagged.
- HubSpot: created deal task HS-4521 and attached MAP and test artifacts.

Attachments: cloudtide_k6_script_v2.js
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CloudTideOnboarding

I'll plan to be on the Jul 9 20:30–23:30 PTO for the run and will post the step-by-step checklist to the Drive tonight. Vivek, let me know if you'd like the rollback runbook to include an automatic model-variant fallback (we can trigger a lighter quantized variant if tail latency climbs).

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
